note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1952. Nominations were received on 20 May 1952: 'POLLING IN the electoral divisions in which there are contests polling day will be Thursday, June 5th' (Strabane Chronicle, 24 May 1952, p. 3) - Thursday 5 June 1952. There were no contests for the county council; the paper prints 'the full list of nominations' with the party labels in brackets. The three changes are Douglas (T. C. Gormley for A. J. Gallagher), Moy (D. S. J. Burrowes for D. E. Gallagher) and Omagh Urban (B. O'Reilly for A. E. Donnelly). Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). The same pattern is visible across this county's rounds. See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt Returned unopposed.
